# Raffica – Roadmap

Overall roadmap of the project. Every milestone is sized so that it can be handled in **one** plan and one round of implementation.

> **This file is generated.** The source is [roadmap.json](roadmap.json) (schema: [roadmap.schema.json](roadmap.schema.json)). Change it only there, then run `dotnet run tools/roadmap.cs -- generate`.

## How we work

1. **"Plan milestone N":** Claude Code reads this roadmap, the linked spec and the current state of the code and writes a plan to `Docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-milestone-NN-<topic>.md`. The plan is linked at the milestone, status → `🟡 planned`.
2. **Implementation:** Work through the plan. Every finished task is ticked right away (`done: true` in `Docs/roadmap.json`).
3. **Completion:** All acceptance criteria checked and ticked → status `✅ done`, enter the date.
4. Scope changes during implementation are recorded under "Scope changes", not silently in the code.

**Status legend:** `⬜ open` · `🟡 planned` · `🔵 in progress` · `✅ done`

**Rules:**
- Work through the milestones in order as a rule. The prerequisites of the respective milestone are what counts.
- A milestone starts with `Create spec` if its subproject has no spec yet. The spec is worked out by brainstorming and put under `Docs/superpowers/specs/`.
- Tasks of later subprojects are deliberately kept rough and are made precise when the respective spec is written.

## Scope changes

- **2026-11-03 (Milestone 0):** M0 includes the import of the Pagewing core (no UI) from the `v1.0.0` tag as the project skeleton: unchanged import, scripted rename, a commit that makes the subset self-contained, and the translation of German text. The listed tasks for the skeleton, `.gitignore` and CI are carried out on top of the imported solution. `.env.example` is not needed because the imported code uses no secrets. Decided in the suite spec and in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` (entry "Core-only import, fresh UI, new order of work").
- **2026-11-03 (Milestone 1.1):** Localized key names in menu shortcuts (`Strg+X` instead of `Ctrl+X`) and the TextBox context menu strings (Fluent's English Cut, Copy and Paste) move to milestone 1.2 with the German layout work. The gallery window is 1520 x 900. Decisions in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entries "Shell project and token conventions (M1.1)" and "Localization mechanism and its limits". The high-contrast palette is a fixed palette, not a token set built from the system colours as the spec asks (entry "High-contrast palette"); owner to confirm.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 1.2):** AppFrame collapses an empty tab row and band, so the start view sits directly under the title bar; the gallery's frame demo gets a fifth File tab.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 1.2):** `AutomationNameTests` ignores the RepeatButtons inside a RangeBase (the zoom slider), which carry no name of their own.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 1.2):** `RibbonView.NotifyInvoked` is new so that `CommandInvoked` also fires for commands run by a field code.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 1.2):** Additions beyond the plan, needed by the frame demo and the reviews: `Pane.IsDocument` and `Pane.PaneName`, `AppFrame.IsLeftPaneShown` and `IsRightPaneShown`, `TitleBar.LeadingInset`, zoom from 10 to 500 percent in steps of 10 with snapping, `FieldCodeTarget`, `PaneFocus.Focus(Pane)` and `StartView.FocusFirstTile`.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 1.2):** Q (search), 6 and 7 (panes) act in the field-code tab-letter stage through app-supplied `FieldCodeTarget`s; the spec lists the badges as display only and the plan said "shows". The group digits stay a display-only legend.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 1.2):** The frame demo window has a minimum width of 1024 px. The full ribbon at 1024 px without the compact bar clips groups of the Home tab; this is a recorded limitation and not a tested case, there is no automatic compact mode (backlog).
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 1.2):** The shell tests run serially (`DisableTestParallelization` in `tests/Raffica.Shell.Tests/TestCulture.cs`) because parallel test classes switching the shared `ShellStrings.Culture` made the suite flaky (about one first run in three after a build).
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2):** Milestones 2.1 to 2.6 are added under the PDF spec: Viewer, Annotate, Forms and signing, Organize pages, Redact, OCR and line editing, Packaging and release. Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entries "Raffica PDF: scope and order (M2)" and "Raffica PDF: speed budgets are measured, not inherited (M2)".
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2):** Milestone 3 (macOS spec) now depends on 2.6 instead of 2, so that macOS stays after the finished PDF app; milestone 2 only means that the PDF spec exists.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2):** The OCR library build moves from the backlog into milestone 2.5, and the release workflow into 2.6; the CodeQL and hardware-measure workflows come back in 2.5. Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: platform code, autosave, OCR build and releases (M2)".
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2):** Milestone 2.1 adds an additive option to the shell's settings dialog so that the PDF app hides the autosave row (autosave contradicts "never damages the original"); the frame's behaviour for the other apps stays as it is. Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: platform code, autosave, OCR build and releases (M2)".
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** Inventory of Pagewing 1.0 (its roadmap and README at the `v1.0.0` tag), entered as marks `(P<n>)` in the tasks of 2.1 to 2.6. Done in 2.1 although not named in the spec's list: document info from the status bar (P4: file, pages, page size, PDF version, file size, metadata) and the F1 help card with the shortcut overview built from the command catalog (P6). Already done in the imported core: `raffica search` (P5). Open for after 2.6 unless the owner asks earlier, both in the backlog: tabs between windows (P4.1) and the "open in new window" command of P4, because the frame's `DocumentTabs` has no drag-out and a workspace across windows is a shell feature that no other app needs yet; the setting "reduce animations" (P6), because the shell's design spec has no such setting and its motion is limited to control transitions (owner to confirm). Not rebuilt on purpose: the density setting (replaced by the compact command bar of the shell) and a separate high-contrast switch (Pagewing followed the system setting as well, and the shell does the same through `ShellTheme.Apply`, so there is nothing to rebuild). Pagewing's public-repository work (12.1) is the owner's decision and stays listed as open in 2.6.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** Three additive extensions of the shell, needed by the PDF app and neutral for the other apps: (1) the settings dialog takes optional `SettingsDialogOptions` (hide the autosave row, extra rows the app builds and reads in its `onOk`), (2) `DocumentTab` gets a dirty marker and an exposed selected state (the selected state of document tabs for assistive technology is done with it, and the backlog item "Accessibility items deferred from the frame" is narrowed to what remains), (3) the frame's `SearchField` takes an optional `ExtraResults` provider for entries that are not ribbon commands (open tabs, recent files, outline entries, "Go to page N"). Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: viewer conventions (M2.1)".
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** A file that is already open is selected, not opened twice (Pagewing opened a second tab). Two tabs of one file would both hold dirty state once 2.2 adds editing.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** The test PDF generator of Pagewing (`tools/make-testpdfs.cs`) is not imported in 2.1: the fixtures under `testdata/pdfs` cover every viewer test, and a task that needs a new fixture says so.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** Milestone 2.1 has 17 tasks in its plan. If the owner asks, it can be split after Task 11 of the plan into 2.1 (viewing and searching) and a further milestone (printing and speed budgets); the extra id is chosen then.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** Additions to the shell made while building 2.1, neutral for the other apps: the status bar zoom range goes up to 800 percent (it was 500; Core allows 800, and above 500 the buttons and the slider drove the zoom backwards), and `CommandDefinition` gets `EnabledWhen` and `DisabledReason` so that a ribbon command can be disabled with a reason (`RibbonView.RefreshCommandStates`; the ribbon did not disable commands before).
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** The Home tab of the PDF ribbon grew to 7 groups and 29 commands (Close tab, Settings, Tabs, Text and Help groups were added); the spec leaves the ribbon content to the app within the frame rules. With no document open, Open, Help and Settings are enabled (the plan said only Open).
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** The Linux print card has no paper-size row: Core's `PrintSettings` has no paper field (the same as Pagewing 1.0), so the printer's default paper is used. The plan item "paper size" is not delivered.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** The settings of PDF follow Core's enums: the page appearance reads "Light / Follow theme" and the default zoom offers three modes (Free is not a valid default).
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** `--settings-file` isolates all of the app's files (`pdf-settings.json` and `recent.json` next to the given file) and the single-instance pipe (its name gets a hash suffix of the path), so a measurement or a test never touches the user's data.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** A file given on the command line at first launch opens at the default position, not at the remembered one: `recent.json` is loaded only after the first sharp page. Measured option for a follow-up: read it in parallel on a pool thread during the open (about 2 ms per run, no effect on the first page); recommended, not adopted. Recorded in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** Naming hygiene: four comments and notes under `bench/` that named the predecessor are reworded to "the predecessor"; the tests keep "Pagewing" only as test data.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** Milestone 2.1 is closed `done` although acceptance criterion 3 (manual check: a file passed as argument and a second file in the running instance) was not checked: the owner skipped it on 2026-11-04. The criterion stays unticked, the automated paths are covered by tests (`InstanceHandoverTests`, `HandoverWindowTests`, `OpenFlowTests`), and the manual check is a backlog entry. The task "Set the PDF speed budgets" is ticked although Chrome was not measured again on the two machines (the M1 numbers stand) and the Windows start-time finding was still open (resolved on 2026-11-04, see the next entry).
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.1):** Software rendering is the Windows default of the PDF app (owner decision of 2026-11-04, after the measurement of runs 41892985596 and 41893002871: every start case halves, idle memory drops to a third, the scroll p99 rises from 13.5 to 18.0 ms). `RAFFICA_RENDERING=default` opts out; Linux and macOS are untouched. The Windows budgets of the PDF target are re-derived from the software medians (cold 200, warm 210, 1000 pages 200, second file 20, scroll p99 20 ms, memory 40, size 51, zip 22 MiB; the old ones, 400/390/400/30/20 ms and 130 MiB, belonged to the GPU path); the Linux budgets stand. Entry "Raffica PDF: software rendering is the Windows default (M2.1 follow-up)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- **2026-11-04 (Milestone 2.2):** The right pane of the PDF app is one marks pane of 256 px (the approved canvas shows a single pane "Markierungen" and no separate comments pane); the empty 300 px comments pane slot of 2.1 is reused for it, and a mark's comment is shown and edited in its entry. The annotate mode of the predecessor is kept (a tool in the Annotate tab starts it, Esc or "Done" ends it); comments are the `/Contents` of a markup or drawing. Not rebuilt from the predecessor's 1.0 feature set because Core has no support for them: sticky notes, reply threads, shape fill, pressure-sensitive width, and a full-rewrite option for annotation saves (annotation saves are incremental only). Entry "Raffica PDF: annotation conventions (M2.2)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`; owner to confirm the marks pane.
- **2026-11-05 (Milestone 2.2):** Changes while building, against the plan and the entry "Raffica PDF: annotation conventions (M2.2)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` (amended there): (a) the tool letters I, R, E, L, A and T are not implemented; the Annotate tab's key tips and the Ctrl+Shift shortcuts exist instead, which avoids another key-capture surface. (b) Colour and width are chosen in an app-side style strip (`Annotating/StyleStrip`) beside the mode badge, not in the ribbon, because the shell ribbon has no checked or swatch control; moving it into the ribbon is a later option. A text box gets colours only on the strip, for a selection. (c) The text-box default font size is 16 pt (Medium, the default of Core and Pagewing 1.0); the plan text said 12. (d) The ribbon shows no checked state for the active tool; the mode badge names the tool and "Esc to finish". (e) Touch input is ignored in annotate mode, because the page view has no touch scrolling yet. (f) The marks pane (256 px, the one right pane) stays flagged "owner to confirm".
- **2026-11-05 (Milestone 2.3):** Departures from the predecessor's forms and signature designs (M11, M12), approved by the owner on 2026-11-05: (1) there is no separate "Fill form" mode; form fields are live whenever the document has fillable fields and no annotate tool is active, and an annotate tool makes them inert. (2) The field highlight is a per-tab switch on a form badge (on by default for a document with fillable fields, not stored); PDFium draws it, the app draws stars for required and locks for read-only fields and the focus ring. (3) The required-field card before saving stays ("Go to first empty field" is the default, "Save anyway" never blocks) and gets a counter on the badge and a "Next required field" command. (4) The notices (calculations and format scripts, XFA, signature fields, buttons) are one dismissible line naming only what applies, not one bar per hint. (5) Core gets `PdfDocument.MayFillFormsAsync` with a Core test, because `MayAnnotateAsync` alone would lock forms of documents that allow only filling. (6) Signing is one step: the Sign command opens the New-signature card when nothing is saved, else a picker card with thumbnails; a pick is placed in the centre of the visible part of the page and selected with the select tool (no ghost under the pointer). Not rebuilt: renaming a saved signature, pasting an image from the clipboard. The signatures folder lies next to `--settings-file` when that switch is given. Entry "Raffica PDF: forms and signing conventions (M2.3)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- **2026-11-05 (Milestone 2.3):** Changes while building, against the plan (details in the amendment of the entry "Raffica PDF: forms and signing conventions (M2.3)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`). Core got four small additions: `PdfDocument.MayFillFormsAsync`, the `GetFormFieldsAsync(int, PdfPriority, ...)` overload, `AnnotationEditor.HasFormChanges` and `PngEncoder.EncodeWithAlpha`. The required-field card is asked for any form change (`HasFormChanges`, which stays true until the next save clears the history, also after the only form step was undone); the form-aware signed-file wording stays tied to `HasOnlyFormChanges`. Every field-editor text box has `AcceptsReturn = true` and no `MaxLength` (the inner text box of an editable combo box keeps Avalonia's default, see the open items), so Avalonia never shortens a pasted text; a pasted break is refused with the one-line hint, instead of the planned `MaxLength` from the field. Added beyond the plan: hover tooltips and composed automation names for locked and required widgets (`FormInteraction`, `FormAutomation`), `FormFocus.PageToLoad` (the walk never jumps an unloaded page, failed page reads are remembered), non-focusable badge buttons, a card when the signature library cannot be read, the Sign group (digit 5, code 51), image signatures that can be moved and scaled (`SelectController.CanChange` tests `SelectionShape`) and Cancel disabled while a signature save is in flight. `NativeBindingsTests` was fixed: `PermissionFillForms` is a PDF-specification bit and is mapped in `SpecificationValues`.
- **2026-11-05 (Milestone 2.4):** Departures from the predecessor's page design (M13) and the author's calls of the plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-05-milestone-02-4-organize-pages.md`, recorded in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` ("Raffica PDF: page organizing conventions (M2.4)"); the owner can overturn single calls: (1) while a page plan is open, the annotate tools, Sign, form filling, Extract, Split and Export images are disabled with the reason "Apply or discard the page changes first" (the output commands read the open document without the plan). (2) Unsaved marks or form values are saved first, after a question; flowing the history into the working copy is not built. (3) The Apply card offers "Save as…" as the default and "Save in the original file" as an armed second choice, lists every loss per kind before anything is written, and says that a rewrite cannot be undone and that no backup copy is made. (4) After a rewrite the app rebuilds the view and panes of the tab (fallback: reopen the written file in the same strip position), because the page list and the page sizes changed. (5) Merge is "Insert file…" into the plan with a page range and a position; the predecessor's merge dialog with a file list stays in the backlog. (6) Extract, Split and Export images are cards with a range field that read the open document; JPEG, crop, watermark, page numbers, page labels, images as pages and dragging pages between tabs stay out as in the predecessor. (7) The ribbon gets a Pages tab (letter P) with the organize, edit, history, apply, output and destructive groups. Milestone 2.5 (redaction) builds on the same rewrite mechanics and the tab rebuild.
- **2026-11-06 (Milestone 2.4):** Changes while building, against the plan (details in the amendment of the entry "Raffica PDF: page organizing conventions (M2.4)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`): the organize mode itself counts as a plan open (also with an identity plan) and locks the annotate tools, Sign, form clicks, keys and commands, marks-pane comments and the output commands; a running save, extract, split or export locks the page commands and the other way round; Save and Save as with a changed plan hand over to the Apply flow through a delegate of `SaveController`; the analysis and rewrite job cards are modal and Apply, Extract, Split and Export images share one `JobRunner` class; closing or discarding a changed plan asks with its own card, and unsaved marks are asked afterwards (a Cancel keeps the plan); the plan version is re-checked before the write; at most 20 files can be inserted per organize session (every registered file counts); a file without pages is refused as unreadable; no `BlankPageCard` was built (a blank page takes the size of its neighbour). Added to earlier code: `OrganizeSession.Ending`, `OrganizeSession.Summarize`, `PdfTab.OrganizeCreated`, `PdfWindow.RebuildTab` and `PdfTab.ResetForRewrittenDocument`. Open: the manual check in an independent viewer and the points in the "Open items" block of milestone 2.4.
- **2026-11-06 (Milestone 2.5):** The ribbon gets two tabs: Redact (letter R, with the destructive group last) and Edit (letter E: edit text lines, recognize text, language files); the right pane shows the redact pane in the marks-pane slot while the mode is on. Pattern search names picture pages and offers OCR, it never starts it. The OCR run is not modal: an options card starts it, a run badge and the status bar show progress with Cancel, a finished run is one unsaved history step. Redaction cleanup stays "not a switch" (owner, 2026-11-06). The OCR library is built here by a dispatch-only workflow on hosted runners and published as the prerelease `native-tesseract-5.5.4-1` of this repository (running it is an owner gate); because the repository is private, `tools/native-fetch.cs` reads the release assets through the GitHub API with a token and keeps the pinned size and SHA-256 as the trust anchor. CodeQL returns, guarded for private repositories; the hardware-measure workflow is the existing `measure.yml` and is not added again. Decisions in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: redaction, OCR and text editing conventions (M2.5)".
- **2026-11-06 (Milestone 2.5 (implementation)):** What changed during implementation against the plan of Milestone 2.5 (details in the amendment of the entry "Raffica PDF: redaction, OCR and text editing conventions (M2.5)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`): `redact-structure` and `redact-objstm` are refused by Core for unremovable page keys and not redacted (the plan text listed them as redactable); the acceptance asserts the refusal. The rescue pages (page as image) join the plan after the picker and the plan-version re-check, not before. Text marks are built as `Kind.Text` marks directly. The retry for a full OCR history was dropped because Core writes the result anyway and reports `Undoable = false`; the app words OCR failures through the new Core type `OcrFailure` because it may not reference `Raffica.Ocr`. Ctrl+Shift+G toggles the whole-line switch of the text-edit field. `ocr.languages` is locked while a run goes, and the recognize card has a "current page" option. Added beyond the plan: `ModeExclusion.CanStart` (the one exception Annotate then Organize), the original-file arming for every alias of the open file, `SetOverlayStyle`, and `AnnotationHistory.HasLiveTextEdits` in Core.

## Milestone 1 – Design directions & spec
**Status:** ✅ done (2026-11-03) · **Plan:** [2026-11-03-milestone-01-design-directions.md](superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-milestone-01-design-directions.md) · **Prerequisites:** M0

Goal: One design direction for all four apps is chosen and the spec for the design system and shell is written.

**Tasks**

- [ ] The updater (P8.1) with its own signing key (kept by the owner in a CI secret) and the release address of this repository; the update-check switch in the settings; the unsaved-changes prompt before an install
- [ ] License notices in the packages and the About card, the release workflow, README for users and CHANGELOG (P8)
- [ ] List the open items that need the owner's machines (installers, printers, the real update key, the public repository) with the command that checks each

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Installers build in CI (the workflow run is named in the evidence)
- [ ] An installed build runs, registers as the PDF handler and updates from one test release to the next with the test key (manual check on Windows and Linux, recorded); the path with the real key stays an open item
- [ ] The release workflow runs green as a dry run (workflow run named in the evidence); publishing the first release is not part of this milestone, it happens only on the owner's instruction and stays listed as an open item
- [ ] Every Pagewing 1.0 feature in the inventory of 2.1 is done or listed as open, with the reason (checked against the inventory by hand and recorded)

## Backlog

Deliberately not planned. Ideas that `/ideen` puts here are listed; if needed, one becomes a milestone.

- **Manual check: independent viewer for merged and split files (2.4):** In Raffica PDF open a temp copy of `testdata/pdfs/pages-marked.pdf`, insert a second file with Insert file in the Pages tab and Save as; split another copy every 2 pages into a folder; open the merged file and one part in an independent viewer, for example Adobe Acrobat Reader, Chrome, Edge or Okular. Expect the page count, the page order and the bookmarks of the main file. Record the viewer's name and version in the "Open items" block of milestone 2.4 and tick its second criterion. The other points not verified here are listed there.
- **Page organizing follow-ups (2.4):** Deferred by the reviews of milestone 2.4: Open after an extract that overwrote a file that is open in another tab selects the stale tab; Cancel stays clickable after the apply has replaced the target (the card says cancelling although the file is replaced); the outline read before the split card cannot be canceled; a non-contiguous selection is gathered at the drop target (documented, a user setting could offer per-page steps); the organize list and `OrganizeThumbnails` repeat logic of `PagesPane` (a shared thumbnail route); stand-in icons for copy and inserted pages; a save started during the flush at mode start is not re-checked before the mode begins.
- **Manual check: independent viewer for filled forms and signatures (2.3):** Core's `InteropSampleTests` write the sample files. Open a temp copy of a PDF with fillable fields in Raffica PDF, fill one field of every kind (text, check box, radio button, list, combo box), place one drawn and one image signature, save, then open the saved file in an independent viewer, for example Adobe Acrobat Reader, Chrome, Edge or Okular. Expect every value and both signatures in place. Record the viewer's name and version in the "Open items" block of milestone 2.3 and tick its second criterion.
- **Manual check: independent viewer for annotated files (skipped for 2.2):** Open a temp copy of a PDF in Raffica PDF, add one mark of every kind (highlight, underline and strike-through, each with a comment; freehand, rectangle, ellipse, line, arrow, text box), save, then open the saved file in an independent viewer, for example Adobe Acrobat Reader, Chrome, Edge or Okular. Expect every mark in place with its colour, width and comment. Record the viewer's name and version, then tick the second acceptance criterion of milestone 2.2. Skipped for milestone 2.2 by the owner on 2026-11-05; the owner makes the manual checks together once Raffica PDF is done. The other points not verified here are listed in the open items of 2.2.
- **Manual check: second file in the running instance (skipped for 2.1):** Start `RafficaPdf.exe --settings-file %TEMP%\rt\s.json testdata\pdfs\text-rich.pdf`, then in a second shell with the same `--settings-file` and a relative path `RafficaPdf.exe --settings-file %TEMP%\rt\s.json hello_world.pdf`: expect exit code 0, one process, the second file as a second tab and the window brought to the front. Skipped for milestone 2.1 by the owner on 2026-11-04; do it with the next release check.
- **ODF and legacy Microsoft formats:** Support for ODF (.odt, .ods, .odp) and the old .doc, .xls and .ppt formats, after the main apps are built.
- **Clean up references to Pagewing documents and translate the fixture catalogue:** About 68 imported files cite Pagewing's German decision-log entries or `packaging/README.md` in comments; the references point at documents that are not in this repo. `testdata/pdfs/LICENSES.md` is still German and describes fixtures generated by `tools/make-testpdfs.cs`, which was not imported. Replace the references with Raffica entries or drop them, translate the catalogue, and decide whether to import or rebuild the test PDF generator.
- **Macros and extensions:** A macro and extension system (a VBA replacement), someday, not for the beginning.
- **Real-time collaboration:** Several people editing one document at the same time, someday, not for the beginning.
- **Automatic compact command bar below a window width:** The full ribbon at 1024 px without the compact bar clips groups of the Home tab; compact mode is a user toggle today. Decide whether the frame switches to compact automatically below a width (a scope change for the frame).
- **What the field-code group numbers should do:** In field-code mode the group digits are shown as a legend only; Q, 6 and 7 act. Decide whether typing a group digit should do something (for example jump to the group).
- **German wording for "System" in the settings dialog:** The German label "Wie System" (`SettingsThemeSystem`, the follow-the-system theme choice) needs the owner's decision on the wording.
- **Ctrl+K and hyperlinks in Write:** The frame binds Ctrl+K to the search field. Word and other editors use Ctrl+K for inserting a hyperlink; settle this in the Write spec (note for the Write spec).
- **Accessibility items deferred from the frame:** Not done in milestone 1.2: the selected state of ribbon tabs is not exposed to assistive technology (only a style class; the document tabs expose it since milestone 2.1), the search results list has no selection semantics, and a document tab has two tab stops (tab and close button).
- **Option key handling on macOS:** A bare Option tap enters field-code mode and takes the next letter; there is no platform gating. Decide the macOS behaviour when the macOS subproject is specified, after checking it on a Mac.
- **Tabs between windows and open in a new window:** Pagewing 1.0 let a tab be moved to its own window (menu "Open in new window", M4) and dragged between windows (M4.1, Windows only). Raffica PDF 2.1 has one window with tabs; the frame's `DocumentTabs` has no drag-out. Revisit after 2.6 or when the owner asks.
- **Setting "reduce animations":** Pagewing 1.0 had it in the settings (M6, because Avalonia had no system setting for it). Raffica's shell has no such setting; add it as an extra row of the settings dialog or as a shell setting once the shell has animations that matter.
- **Remove the overlap between Core and Shell settings:** Core's `AppSettings` still has `Theme`, `Language` and `Density`, which the shell settings (`ShellSettings`) own; the PDF app does not read them. Remove the fields or migrate them so that two files cannot disagree.
- **PDF app: command states and icons:** Toggle commands (dark page, panes) have no checked state; add a shell `CheckedWhen` like `EnabledWhen`. Missing shell icons: printer, gear, up and left chevrons, moon, copy; the ribbon uses the least misleading placeholders. Disabled ribbon buttons are not focusable, so the reason (for example for print) shows on hover only; expose it as help text.
- **PDF app: pane and print card accessibility:** The outline is a flat list with depth in the automation name, not a tree with levels in the accessibility tree; there is no visible pane switcher (ribbon group and shortcuts switch); the print job card has no live region or real progress element.
- **Print follow-ups:** Cancelling during the CUPS submit still prints (the submit call, cupsPrintFile2, cannot be cancelled and the app does not call cupsCancelJob2 afterwards: add it and test it on a Linux machine, see DECISIONS, viewer deviations). Failed pages are lost if the job is cancelled afterwards.
- **Search and selection follow-ups:** The selection highlight is lost when Core's page-text cache (32 pages) evicts a page. An unhandled `TileFailed` leaves a page on its preview.
- **Speed follow-ups of the viewer:** Read `recent.json` in parallel with the first open so that a command-line file opens at its remembered position (about 2 ms per run). Per-frame allocations in `PageView.Replan` and `DrawPage` (a `Pen` per page, LINQ in the planner) are small on the dev VM; re-check the scroll case on real GPU machines before changing them.
- **Annotate keys: possible latent routing problem (M2.2):** `AnnotateInteraction` uses a bubble handler gated on `!Handled`, so the arrow keys of a selected mark may be consumed by `PageView`'s class handler first. The redact mode had exactly this bug in M2.5 and uses a tunnel handler now. Check the annotate mode with a routed key test (a real key event through the window) before changing anything.
- **OCR run lock is window-wide:** `OcrBusy` disables Save and Print in every tab while a text-recognition run goes, not only in the tab that is being recognized. It is the existing design of the busy lists; a per-tab rule needs the save and print flows to ask the tab.
- **Redaction of files with unremovable page keys:** Any file with `/Thumb`, `/PieceInfo`, `/Metadata` or `/AA` on any page is refused by Core and gets no rescue (`redact-structure`, `redact-objstm`). Turning the offending page into an image would drop the keys but is a design question for the owner: which pages may be turned into pictures without asking, and what the card says.
- **Redaction analysis time for 1000 pages (13.8 s measured):** The analysis step before the Apply card took 13.8 s for `thousand-pages.pdf` with one area mark per page, and the rewrite and check 15.2 s (single run, see `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "... measurements (M2.5)"). Look at what the analysis does per page (reading and measuring every page) and whether it can skip unmarked pages; re-measure on the owner's machines first.
- **Run the native build workflow again after a version bump:** Steps: bump the versions in the build files (`versions.txt`), dispatch `.github/workflows/native-tesseract.yml` (`gh workflow run native-tesseract.yml -f build=1`, the workflow must exist on the default branch), copy the sizes and SHA-256 of the job summary into the pins of `tools/native-fetch.cs`, update the tests that name them, run `dotnet run tools/native-fetch.cs -- selftest` and the OCR tests with `RAFFICA_REQUIRE_OCR=1`. Running it is an owner gate.
- **Predecessor's open items worth keeping:** From the predecessor's M14 to M16 designs and not built in 2.5: a code list of overlay text ("blocks") for repeated labels; `/Redact` annotation markers so marks survive a save before Apply; QPDF post-processing of the written file; OSD and deskew for OCR; removing an imported language file from the app; reuse of the embedded replacement font for edited text; keep-lists for bookmarks and forms that point into redacted pages.
- **Text edit: vertical lines, field rotation, Tab across unloaded pages:** The text edit mode does not handle vertical writing, sizes the field for rotated pages only approximately, and Tab walks only the pages whose runs are loaded (the focus never jumps over an unloaded page). Ctrl+Shift+G is not in the command catalog or the help card, so it is announced only when the switch changes.
- **A dedicated OCR permission reason:** The gate of `ocr.run` for a locked file reuses the wording of the annotate lock ("annotations"); give it its own reason text in both languages.
- **Print with pending redaction marks prints the unredacted pages:** Plan call 2 says "Print stays" in the redact mode, so a print while marks are pending prints the pages as they are, without the marks applied. Owner decision: add a note on the print card while marks are pending (and say what is printed), or lock print like Save.
- **Native build workflow: split build and upload permissions:** `.github/workflows/native-tesseract.yml` builds and uploads with one job that needs `contents: write`. Split the build (`contents: read`) from the upload job (`contents: write`) so the third-party source builds without a write token, and fix the header comment that names a `release.yml` that does not exist.
- **Scan hint reappears after a redact or organize rebuild:** `PdfTab.ResetForRewrittenDocument` drops `ScanHintHandled`, so "Not now" and "Don't ask again for this file" are forgotten after an Apply that rebuilds the tab. Keep the flag for the same file across the rebuild.
- **TextEditSession.cs is 939 lines:** `src/Raffica.Pdf/TextEditing/TextEditSession.cs` holds the runs, the draft, the preview and the commit. Split candidate: the commit and the old-text note from the reading of the runs.
- **Duplicated preamble of the mode starters:** `ToggleOrganizeAsync`, `ToggleRedactAsync`, `ToggleTextEditAsync` and `StartOcrRunAsync` repeat the same preamble (flush an open field edit and a typed comment of the marks pane, re-check the locks afterwards). Extract one helper with a test per mode.
